svg.title: Four structurally different recipes for generating a new sample
svg.desc: Four panels, each describing a different generative model family through a painting metaphor: an autoregressive model painting one brushstroke at a time from a real probability distribution, a GAN as a forger competing against a critic, a VAE compressing a painting to a short code and expanding it back, and a diffusion model cleaning static into a picture over many steps.
svg.text: Four ways to learn to produce something new
Autoregressive: one stroke at a time
Each stroke chosen from a real probability
distribution over what comes next, given all prior strokes.
Forger paints quickly; critic tries to catch fakes.
Forger improves only by fooling the critic, never directly.
Every painting reduced to a short, structured description.
New paintings come from a new description, expanded back.
Diffusion: clean static into a picture
Starts from pure static, removes a little noise at a time.
Trained only by learning to undo noise added to real data.
Four structurally different recipes for the same goal: producing a new sample that looks like it
